# Apuleius — Psyche et Cupido (Purser, 1913)

[Source index](../../../README.md) · [Reading entrance](../../../../../../README.md) · [48 movements](../../../../../../section-rooms/README.md)

**Shortened note:** Apuleius,*Psyche et Cupido*, 6.21.3.

**Bibliography:** Apuleius.*Psyche et Cupido*.Edited by Louis C. Purser. London: P. H. Lee Warner for the Medici Society, 1913. https://faculty.georgetown.edu/jod/apuleius/cupid.html.

The title is transcribed from the selected Latin object's heading. Do not substitute Purser's other commentary editions, Gaselee 1915, or an unidentified modernized English text.

## Essay use and narrative integrity

The primary tale supplies `mytheme-eros-psyche`, admitted as a supplementary plate at `submission-package/essay/symbolon/mytheme/worlds/roman-latin/eros-psyche/WHOLE.md`. It bears the A13/A23 trust relation and A20/A27's image/possession and unity distinction. Its place remains supplementary; this source house does not promote it over the Ares–Aphrodite–Harmonia whole.

The project's union-without-merger operation is Argued in its native register. Apuleius is evidence for the tale, not an external proof of that operation. The closing legal possession idiom remains a material friction to be carried, not translated into an assertion that Apuleius himself rejected possession. Four tasks cannot stand for the whole, and a formal four/six relation cannot be established by merely counting them.

## Material metadata and full-read provenance

- **Selected object:** Georgetown's Project Libellus text explicitly identifies Purser, Lee Warner, Medici Society, London 1913 in its heading and Richard Clay/Jacobi printing information in its colophon. Full Latin tale covers 4.28–6.24.
- **Read coverage:** all 65, 571 normalized text characters, in four contiguous nontruncated reads 0–17000, 17000–34000, 34000–51000, 51000–end, 2026-09-06. Header and colophon included. Raw HTML acquisition hash is recorded in the working acquisition addendum. No full text stored in the canonical house.
- **Locator alignment:** [BCS whole-story plan](https://bcs.fltr.ucl.ac.be/apul/amorplan.html) provides chapter/subsection divisions; [6.16.2–21.4](https://bcs.fltr.ucl.ac.be/apul/amor12.html) and [6.22.1–24.4](https://bcs.fltr.ucl.ac.be/apul/amor13.html) checked directly for card alignment. This separately identified French witness supplies navigation, not the selected Latin wording.
- **English:** Pomona's complete booksIV–VI offer reading assistance but their modernization's edition is unverified. No English quotation is certified by this Latin house. Named English-edition acquisition remains Open.
- **Frame:** the selected excerpt begins 4.28 and ends 6.24. It does not include the old-woman/captive/Lucius framing passages outside those bounds; whole-novel frame quotation remains a separate acquisition task.
- **NOTES:** absent; none created. Typographical join/split defects elsewhere in the Libellus text require caution for future long quotations; the short cards below were checked in their local sentences.

## Passages and excerpts

<a id="apuleius-1913-psyche-cupido-purser-q001"></a>
## Passage card — `apuleius-1913-psyche-cupido-purser-q001` — the relation before its exposure
^apuleius-1913-psyche-cupido-purser-q001

Beauty displaces Venus's worship; the oracle sends Psyche to exposure. Zephyr brings her to the unseen household. Her sisters cultivate suspicion; lamp and blade expose Cupid, and burning oil drives separation.

- **Locator:**4.28–5.24; revelation 5.21.3–23.5; flight 5.23.6–24.5.
- **Status:** paraphrase-ready; no English source quotation.
- **Verification:** complete selected Latin read 2026-09-06; chapter route compared with BCS plan.
- **Source relation:** paraphrased.
- **Evidential action:** supports the whole relational prehistory.
- **Consumers:** `mytheme-eros-psyche`; A13; A20; A23.
- **Use boundary:** Psyche's action includes attempted violence and bodily curiosity; do not reduce it to a neutral request for evidence.

<a id="apuleius-1913-psyche-cupido-purser-q002"></a>
## Passage card — `apuleius-1913-psyche-cupido-purser-q002` — the helpers and return conditions
^apuleius-1913-psyche-cupido-purser-q002

Pan intervenes; sisters perish; divine sanctuary fails. Venus imposes tasks: ants sort grain, a reed directs fleece collection, an eagle obtains water, and a tower prescribes descent and return. The return needs reserved payments and refusal of deceptive appeals.

- **Locator:**5.25–6.20; grain 6.10.1–11.2; fleece 6.11.3–13.1; water 6.13.2–16.1; descent 6.16.2–20.6.
- **Status:** paraphrase-ready.
- **Verification:** full Latin read 2026-09-06; BCS chapter divisions checked.
- **Source relation:** paraphrased.
- **Evidential action:** supports whole-task structure; qualifies self-sufficient achievement.
- **Consumers:** `mytheme-eros-psyche`; A23; A27.
- **Use boundary:** helpers do not prove a generic universal developmental ladder; the native Return obligation needs this particular narrative and its asymmetries.

<a id="apuleius-1913-psyche-cupido-purser-q003"></a>
## Passage card — `apuleius-1913-psyche-cupido-purser-q003` — waking by the arrow
^apuleius-1913-psyche-cupido-purser-q003

> Psychen innoxio punctulo sagittae suae suscitat

- **Locator:**6.21.3; whole episode 6.21.1–4.
- **Status:** Latin digital quotation-ready; print-image collation Open.
- **Verification:** exact seven-word substring transcribed and reread in selected Libellus object 2026-09-06; BCS6.21.3 confirms episode/subsection alignment.
- **Source relation:** extracted.
- **Evidential action:** corrects a kiss substitution.
- **Consumers:** `mytheme-eros-psyche`; A23.
- **Use boundary:** after the box releases sleep, Cupid removes it and wakes Psyche with a harmless arrow prick. This is not an English-edition quotation or proof of a psychological mechanism.

<a id="apuleius-1913-psyche-cupido-purser-q004"></a>
## Passage card — `apuleius-1913-psyche-cupido-purser-q004` — union and the legal idiom
^apuleius-1913-psyche-cupido-purser-q004

> sic rite Psyche convenit in manum Cupidinis

- **Locator:**6.24.4; settlement 6.22–24; immortality 6.23.5, not 6.24.
- **Status:** Latin digital quotation-ready; print-image collation Open.
- **Verification:** exact eight-word substring reread 2026-09-06; aligned against BCS6.24.4. Pomona's alternative placement of some material under 24 is not followed.
- **Source relation:** extracted; the philosophical operation is argued from the complete tale.
- **Evidential action:** supports union while qualifying a false attribution of anti-possession doctrine.
- **Consumers:** `mytheme-eros-psyche`; A27; A23.
- **Use boundary:** legal marriage, immortality and Voluptas conclude the tale. Its possession language remains visible; a modern juridical claim about Roman marriage requires separate legal evidence.
